en: The Prayer of Benediction to the Blessed Lady Nairātmyā: Oṃ, homage to Śrī Nairātmyā!
She who severs the afflictions and the like, bearing a radiance resembling the splendor of the sun, with her right hand raised...
May Nairātmyā— who transcends the extremes of existence and non-existence, who is free from the heat of passion, who destroys Māra,
and who is endowed with four variegated wheels at her private parts, heart, throat, and the region of her crown— grant you always an incomparable bliss of peace, she who is of fierce form. (1)
She who brings happiness to people by the sound of the bells on her radiant *khaṭvāṅga*, who has burnt away the wicked with the rays of her eyes,
whose nature is the *āli-kāli* of wisdom and means, who bears a garland of human heads, whose body is bent in reverence,
who makes her dwelling in the moon-disk of the mind during deep sleep, she too performs the dance upon her cross-legged seat.
May the Mother of the assembly of Victors, whose nature is selfless bliss and who destroys all sins, protect you! ||2||

The *tāṇḍava* dance of the Goddess Nairātmikā— who possesses that [power], who steals the hearts of the *sajjiṇas*, who strikes terror into the wicked, and whose face is like a sapphire or collyrium darkened by wine— is victorious;
she stands within the interior of a blue lotus like a curved flash of lightning, intensely radiant and exceedingly sharp.
May she who cuts down and destroys all obstacles pacify the impurities of our body, speech, and mind. (3)
From fear, [he is] one who bears Rudra; he possesses the essence of the Vasus of the day; he is the Sādhya; he is the world devoid of sound;
he is called the Luminous One (*Ābhāsvara*); he has stolen the body of the Niṣitaka; his activity is beyond the sun; indeed, he is without sound;
he is free from the great kings of the Mahārājikas; he is the protector of the *Ragla* (or *Ratna*) Rākṣasas.
May the dancing Nairātmikā, who moves with terrifying gait, always be the dispeller of fear for you. ||4||
Dancing with the nine incomparable sentiments, laughing with loud, boisterous laughter, black in color,
wearing a discus, earrings, a necklace, armlets, and a beautiful girdle-string; holding a skull-bowl and a knife in her raised, tawny-colored hands, she resounds with sound.
May Nairātmyā, accompanied by Capalā and like a row of clouds filled with cranes, protect you. ||5||
Because the goddess Nairātmyā, whose luster surpasses that of split kajjala, herself placed this white lotus in her left hand as she approached him,
its interior became red with blood, fulfilling his innermost desire.
It shines like a casket situated between the play-lotuses of the moon and the sun. ||6||

Situated on the left is the one called Lalanā, carrying water, a portion of Prajñā, and the nature of emptiness (śūnyatā); situated on the right is the one called Rasanā, carrying semen, whose essence is compassion (kāruṇya).
But situated in the middle is Avadhūtī, carrying the intoxicating [nectar], which is non-dual in its undifferentiated form.
May that Blessed Lady Nairātmikā, who takes the form of the three channels, protect you! ||7||
This concludes the hymn of benediction for the Blessed Lady Nairātmyā.
